title: Choose LanTube's visual world
question: The roll assigned the Lobby Name Panel. Keep it, take an alternate, or re-roll.

options.label: Lobby Name Panel
options.lineage: European apartment-entry buzzer panels: brass plate, engraved name strips, lit bell buttons
options.thesis: LanTube is the house's front door: every resident's channel is an engraved name strip, lit when they've posted something you haven't seen.
options.viewport: Brass directory rail of residents' name strips (lit = new) beside the feed: Continue watching, New in the house, then each resident's shelf.
options.risk: If the brass is overdone it becomes a costume; it must stay a rail and strips, never skeuomorphic screws everywhere.

raised.raise: Amber is reserved for one job, your own trail: unseen lights and resume bars only, never decoration.
The directory packs tight: every name strip is the same box on a strict hairline grid, no whitespace inflation.
The header's guide line names the span in view (e.g. 'New in the house · Mia'), recomputed as you scroll.
One module governs everything: strips, thumbnails and gaps snap to the panel's grid.
Total palette commitment: no stray greys, every neutral is either lacquer, brass, or engraving ink.

options.label: Family Wall Calendar
options.lineage: kitchen wall calendars and chore charts, one marker colour per person
options.thesis: Every person in the house owns a colour, and that colour follows their videos everywhere.
options.viewport: Week-strip of recent uploads coloured by owner across the top, then colour-keyed shelves per person.
options.risk: Familiar: per-person colour coding is common in family-organiser apps, and colour may fight thumbnails.

options.label: Streaming Title Wall
options.lineage: streaming catalog walls of horizontally scrolling poster rows
options.thesis: Rows of thumbnails; the one you land on grows and tells you what it is while the rest dims.
options.viewport: Featured video band, then rails: Continue watching, New in the house, one rail per channel.
options.case: Wins product clarity (reads instantly as a video site, great on TV), loses audience identification: it feels like Netflix, not the household.
options.risk: Generic: dark ground plus one accent is the category default.

options.label: Orienteering Map
options.thesis: Terrain colours beneath, the course in purple above.
options.viewport: Videos as controls on a course.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a household doesn't navigate its videos like terrain; clarity suffers.
options.kept: A colour reserved for exactly one job: your own trail.
options.risk: Reads as a map, not a video site.

options.label: Japanese High-Density Web
options.thesis: Hairline-boxed modules packed edge to edge.
options.viewport: A dense mosaic of video modules.
options.case: Fuses poorly: too dense for a TV across the room; no household identity.
options.kept: Density courage: equal boxes on a strict hairline grid.

options.label: Lexicon Page
options.thesis: Guide words name the span you're inside; colour lives only in plates.
options.case: Fuses poorly: bookish, not a family video site.
options.kept: Guide words: the header names the span in view.

options.label: Crouwel Grid Specimen
options.thesis: The visible construction grid is the design.
options.viewport: Monumental grid lettering over a catalog.
options.case: Fuses poorly: a poster, not a household.

options.label: Datamatics Field
options.thesis: Pure black and white barcode fields.
options.case: Fuses poorly: hostile to thumbnails and to a family audience.
options.kept: Total palette commitment, no stray greys.
options.risk: Strobing art piece, not a video site.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A video site home executed impeccably: thumbnail grid, left nav, topic chips.
canonCard.viewport: Search bar on top, left nav, chips, a 4-column grid of thumbnails.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from the platforms it copies, which you said would feel wrong.
